answer: The lichen plots are photographed every year, and the growth of each crust is measured to the millimetre against the last photograph. A beacon plot claimed as measured fails the photographs: the lichen must have grown on the rock at the thread of the year, and a plot never measured has no growth to show. Buying a false growth record costs a forger 6,700 in bribes to the surveyor and fees to the station, and the forge photographs are kept in the archive, so a plot whose growth was never measured is seen as bare rock.
